solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Second blast outside is very close

indicators.note: the word for a blast sits outside, wrapping around the abbreviation for second

parts.note: a blast is a loud BOOM

explanation.surface: A second explosion goes off dangerously near.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosom friends are intimate ones, so the adjective conveys being extremely intimate.

clue.text: One scorer surprisingly able, another satisfactory

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters of able appear in an unexpected order

parts.note: another scorer, i.e. composer: Lionel Bart, who wrote the musical Oliver!
OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: Comparing two composers: one unexpectedly capable, the other merely adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' means a composer of musical scores, not a goal-getter; 'another' leans on it to mean a second composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bartok was a Hungarian composer, and a composer writes scores.

clue.text: Southern Greek character raised total

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means the letters read upwards, i.e. reversed

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A southern Greek figure has increased the total.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is the amount you get by adding numbers together.

clue.text: Byron's end portrayed in melancholy lament

indicators.note: the final letter is depicted within the gloomy word, placed inside it

parts.note: moody means melancholy

indicators.note: end takes the last letter of Byron's name

explanation.surface: Lord Byron's death depicted in a sad elegy.
explanation.definitionFit: A monody is an ode of mourning sung by one voice, an elegy.

clue.text: Plant in estate well clear of borders

parts.note: the grounds of a house are its estate

indicators.note: the word well is stripped of its outer letters, keeping only the inside

explanation.surface: A gardener spots a plant growing on an estate, comfortably away from the flower borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common yellow-flowered weed of the daisy family.

clue.text: Petersham's much-admired film?

parts.note: something great is highly regarded
a film is a thin coat or layer

explanation.surface: Asks whether Petersham is the subject of a celebrated movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but means a thin layer; a petersham is a heavy overcoat named after Viscount Petersham.
explanation.definitionFit: A petersham is a heavy overcoat of thick woollen cloth, a type of long winter coat.

clue.text: Love line and false statement seen in Hardy?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, hence O
a lie is a false statement

explanation.surface: Romance, plot and deceit in a Thomas Hardy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' suggests Thomas Hardy the novelist, but it is Oliver Hardy of Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Hardy, the comic actor, was known familiarly as Ollie; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Port not vintage — enjoy last of Semillon

parts.note: something new is not old or vintage
to have can mean to enjoy, as in having a good time

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of Semillon

explanation.surface: A wine buff dismisses a young port in favour of the remains of the Semillon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine, but it is a harbour town: Newhaven, a ferry port in Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Newhaven is a harbour town on the English south coast with ferries to France.

clue.text: Stay in order to see well-camouflaged creature

parts.note: to stick is to stay put
a sect is a religious order or group

explanation.surface: Advice to keep still and look carefully to spot a hidden creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Stick insects look like twigs, and that disguise hides them from predators.

clue.text: Barge capsized shown in national emblem

indicators.note: in a down entry a capsized word is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge

explanation.surface: A barge turns over and appears in a national symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is the national emblem of Wales, worn on St David's Day.

clue.text: Worthless person, erstwhile Prime Minister, shows zest

parts.note: a lemon is slang for a useless person or dud
Sir Robert Peel was British Prime Minister in the 1830s and 1840s

explanation.surface: A dismissive put-down of a former Prime Minister who nonetheless shows energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zest' looks like enthusiasm, but here it is the grated rind of citrus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the outer rind of citrus fruit used for flavouring in cooking.

clue.text: Horse served in Bordeaux perhaps causing belly-ache

indicators.note: the horse letter is put inside the drink, as if served in a glass

parts.note: Bordeaux is an example of a wine
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A horse is given claret and ends up with stomach pains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belly-ache' is the informal word for a grumble, not a stomach complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellyache is slang for complaining peevishly, the same as a whine as a moan.

clue.text: What's unimportant as compared with former currency?

parts.note: beside can mean in comparison with, as in 'beside her, he looks tiny'
the mark was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Asking what counts as trivial when set against an obsolete currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beside the mark misses the point, so it is irrelevant and of no consequence.

clue.text: Stench terrible with decay in New York City

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are mangled into a different order

explanation.surface: A dreadful smell of rot in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Schenectady is a city in the state of New York, near Albany.

clue.text: Group for example, east European, appearing in Greek city

indicators.note: the abbreviations show up inside the name of the Greek city

parts.note: Thebes is an ancient city in Greece

explanation.surface: A band, say, with an east European, appearing in a Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go between THEBE and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bee Gees were a pop group of three brothers, the Gibbs.

clue.text: Lying between two rivers, what was that industrial region?

indicators.note: the exclamation sits between the two river letters, enclosed by them

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, taken twice
uh? is a puzzled query, like asking what was that

explanation.surface: A geography question about an industrial area sandwiched between two rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is Germany's great coal and steel district in the west of the country.

clue.text: Youth in the quarter for Valentine's Day?

indicators.note: the young person goes inside the word for a quarter

parts.note: a quarter is a fourth part
a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: A young person in the town district on Valentine's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: the date, not the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Valentine's Day falls on the fourteenth of February, so the ordinal names that date.

clue.text: Collar on dogs or catlike mammals

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the collar word comes first

parts.note: a ring round the neck is a collar
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: Collars placed on dogs or cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogs' is a verb meaning follows, not the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringtails are raccoon relatives such as the cacomistle, sometimes called ring-tailed cats.

clue.text: Son left in club to speak explosively

indicators.note: the left letter goes inside the golf club word

parts.note: a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A son, left inside a club, starts ranting.
explanation.definitionFit: To splutter is to talk in a hasty, spitting way, as when angry or flustered.

clue.text: Almighty muddle in poem not finally relevant

indicators.note: a muddle is a jumble, so these letters are mixed up into a new order
finally takes only the closing letter of the word relevant

explanation.surface: An exclamation of frustration at a confused poem that ends up being irrelevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddle' scrambles IN, POEM and NOT into OMNIPOTEN; the last letter of 'relevant' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Almighty is God, all-powerful, which is what omnipotent describes.

clue.text: Auntie coming back just the same?

definitions.meaning: Auntie is a British nickname for the BBC
a word that is just the same coming back reads identically backwards, a palindrome

explanation.surface: An aunt returns home unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' and 'the Beeb' are both British nicknames for the BBC, and BEEB is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Auntie is an affectionate nickname for the British Broadcasting Corporation, as is the Beeb.

clue.text: With short sudden movement snake gets rodent

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its final letter

parts.note: a jerk is a sudden movement
a boa is a constricting snake

explanation.surface: A snake lunges suddenly and catches a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The jerboa is a small desert rodent that hops on long hind legs.

clue.text: Deer that transformed stops car in dramatic event

indicators.note: the jumbled letters plug the gap within the car word, as a stopper does

parts.note: a coupe is a two-door car

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A transformed deer halts a car, which would be quite a dramatic event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' reads as halts, but means plugs: the anagram DETHEATR, signalled by 'transformed', fills the gap in the car word.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup de theatre is a sudden sensational turn in a play, or any striking surprise.

clue.text: Spider-Man's inner skin layer

indicators.note: inner says the letters lie inside the name, spanning its middle

explanation.surface: A comment on the comic-book hero's inner layer of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The derma is the dermis, the layer of skin beneath the epidermis.

clue.text: Almost entirely lecherous American writer

indicators.note: almost entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: randy is British slang for lustful

explanation.surface: Describes a US author as nearly wholly lustful.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayn Rand was a Russian-born American novelist, author of Atlas Shrugged.

clue.text: At sea stop son boarding a vessel

indicators.note: the son letter gets aboard, going inside the vessel phrase

parts.note: a vat is a large container

explanation.surface: A sailor's order to halt as a son climbs aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is the nautical command to cease, used aboard ship.

clue.text: Hanger-on in French city initially expecting pay back

indicators.note: the clinging seed case goes inside the name of the French city

parts.note: Reims is a city in the Champagne region of France
a bur clings to clothing, hence a hanger-on

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of expecting

explanation.surface: A sponger in a French city is expecting to be repaid.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse is to refund money someone has spent.

clue.text: One's mad having lost this cleaning cloth

definitions.meaning: to lose one's ... is a British idiom for losing one's temper, becoming mad
an old piece of cloth for cleaning

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about losing their duster.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a scrap of fabric used for wiping, and losing it idiomatically means getting angry.

clue.text: Dad's Army cast entertaining English illusions

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold, so the scrambled words take in the English letter
cast can mean throw into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The cast of the British sitcom Dad's Army entertaining an English audience with illusions.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a long-running British TV comedy about the wartime Home Guard; 'cast' reworks its letters around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Daydreams are pleasant fantasies, imaginings that are not real.

clue.text: Serviceman in receding tide finds protection

indicators.note: the soldier goes inside the reversed water word
receding means moving backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the tide is the sea, loosely
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier caught by an ebbing tide finds safety.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the aegis of means under the protection or sponsorship of; the aegis was Zeus's shield.
